arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Loeb argued the government seeks to transform a contract violation into a constitutional waiver.
Mr. Feigin argued the side that brought the case must prove a connection to the car to claim privacy rights.
Mr. Loeb stated the government's claim that the driver violated criminal law is incorrect.
Mr. Feigin questioned the validity of claiming privacy in a vehicle one is not allowed to drive.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of Fourth Amendment protections in rental vehicles. The core issue is whether a contractual clause waives privacy rights for drivers not listed on the rental agreement.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between private contracts and constitutional rights. It determines whether rental companies can waive driver privacy through standard agreements. The outcome shapes police search powers in shared vehicles. It impacts millions of drivers who use rental cars. It clarifies the scope of Fourth Amendment protections in commercial contexts.
